# Plan a Week of Social Media Posts with AI: A Small-Business Guide

> **In short:** Give an AI assistant a one-paragraph brief about your business, your audience, and the week's theme, and it will draft seven ready-to-edit social posts with hashtag ideas, suggested posting times, and image prompts. You'll still edit and approve everything — AI does the blank-page work, you keep the voice.

If running a small business already eats your Mondays, social media is probably the task you keep putting off. This guide walks you through a repeatable routine: you write a short brief once, an AI assistant turns it into a full week of posts, and you spend the rest of your morning reviewing instead of inventing.

## Before you start
- **An account with any general-purpose AI assistant** (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Le Chat, or similar — pick whichever you already have). Free plans are fine for this task.
- **Three things to write down before you open the AI**: (1) what your business sells in one sentence, (2) who your typical customer is, and (3) the theme or focus for the week ahead.
- **About 30 minutes total.** Roughly 10 minutes writing the brief, 15 minutes reviewing the draft, 5 minutes scheduling or copying into your scheduler.
- **A plain text document** (Notes, Google Doc, or even an email draft) where you'll paste the AI's output so you can edit it in one place.

## Step 1 — Open a fresh chat and write your brief
Open your AI assistant and start a **new conversation** — don't reuse an old chat, because old context can confuse the assistant about your new week. In the first message, type a short brief that covers three things: what your business does, who you're talking to, and what the week's posts should focus on. If you don't see a "New chat" button, look for one labeled **New conversation**, **Reset**, or a pencil/edit icon at the top of the chat list.
💬 Example: "I'm the owner of a small home-bakery called Crumb & Crust. My customers are mostly busy parents in their 30s and 40s who order weekend treat boxes. This week's theme is 'back-to-school lunchbox treats' — I want 7 posts (one per day, Monday to Sunday) for Instagram and Facebook. Tone: friendly, warm, a little playful. Each post should have a caption, 5–8 hashtag ideas, a suggested posting time, and a short image or photo idea."
You'll know it worked when the assistant replies with a structured week of posts — usually seven numbered blocks with captions, hashtags, times, and image notes.

## Step 2 — Ask for the format that fits your channels
Before you accept the first draft, tell the assistant the exact platforms you use and the post length that feels natural. Most small businesses post a mix of short updates and slightly longer stories, and the AI will adjust if you say so. Look for the chat input box at the bottom of the screen; type a follow-up message that names your platforms and any limits (like "Instagram captions under 150 words" or "LinkedIn should sound more professional").
💬 Example: "Please rewrite the captions so Instagram ones are under 150 words and feel casual, and add 2 LinkedIn-friendly versions of the Wednesday and Friday posts for my bakery's business page. Keep hashtags at the end of each caption."
You'll know it worked when the assistant rewrites the relevant posts in the new style, and you can spot the platform difference by reading just one caption aloud.

## Step 3 — Request hashtag groups you can rotate
Hashtags go stale fast if you use the same ten every week, and AI is good at producing fresh, themed batches. In the same chat, ask the assistant to **group your hashtags into three rotating sets** — one for product posts, one for behind-the-scenes posts, one for community or customer posts. This way you don't reuse the same block every day and your reach stays varied. If your assistant offers a "pin" or "favorite" option for this message, pin it so you can refer back next week.
💬 Example: "Group my hashtags into three sets I can rotate: (A) product-focused like #weekendbaking #lunchboxideas, (B) behind-the-scenes like #smallbakery #handmade, (C) community like #supportlocal #busyparents. Give me 6 hashtags per set."
You'll know it worked when the assistant returns three clearly labeled groups, each with about six hashtags that all feel on-brand for your business.

## Step 4 — Get image or photo ideas you can actually shoot
A caption without a visual feels half-finished, so ask the assistant to add a one-sentence image idea to each post — something a phone camera can capture in a few minutes. Look for the assistant's reply under your last message; below each post there should now be a short "Image idea" or "Visual:" line. If your screen looks crowded, scroll within the reply — the ideas are usually tucked under each numbered post.
💬 Example: "For each of the 7 posts, add a one-sentence image idea I can photograph myself with a phone — keep props simple (a lunchbox, a cutting board, a kid's backpack) and avoid anything that needs a studio."
You'll know it worked when you can read the seven image ideas in under a minute and picture exactly what to shoot for each one — no idea should require props you don't own.

## Step 5 — Edit in your own voice and save the week
The AI's draft is the starting point, not the final post. Copy the whole thing into the text document you prepared earlier, then read each caption out loud and tweak anything that doesn't sound like you — swap a word, shorten a sentence, add a local reference. This is the step most people skip, and it's the one that makes the posts feel real instead of generic. After editing, save the file as "Social week of [date]" so next week you can start from last week's pattern.
💬 Example: Your edited Monday caption might end up reading "Lunchbox heroes wanted — and yes, there's chocolate involved. This week's boxes are built for the 7am rush. DM to reserve yours by Thursday." instead of the AI's first draft.
You'll know it worked when you read all seven posts back-to-back and they feel like they came from the same person — you.

## Step 6 — Schedule or copy into your posting tool
Now put the posts where they'll actually go live. If you use a scheduler like Buffer, Later, or Meta Business Suite, paste each post into the right day and time slot; if you don't, just leave them in your text document with the date next to each one. Look for a **calendar**, **compose**, or **new post** button in your scheduler — the words vary, but the action is the same: paste caption, add image when ready, pick the date. Some schedulers also have an "AI assist" or "best time to post" hint built in; use that to cross-check the times the AI suggested.
💬 Example: After pasting, your Monday row in the scheduler reads: caption about lunchbox treats, hashtags at the end, posting time Tuesday 8:15 AM (because the AI suggested mornings for busy parents and your scheduler confirmed that's a high-activity slot).
You'll know it worked when every day of the week has a post sitting in its slot, with a caption, hashtags, and an image idea ready — and you can stop thinking about social media until next Monday.

## Common mistakes
- **Skipping the edit step.** AI captions often sound polished but generic. The fix: always read each one out loud and rewrite at least one sentence per post in your own words.
- **Using the same brief for every platform.** Instagram and LinkedIn audiences expect different tones. The fix: in Step 2, ask for platform-specific versions and never cross-post the exact same caption everywhere.
- **Trusting hashtag lists without checking.** Some AI assistants invent hashtags that look real but have very few posts behind them. The fix: paste each new hashtag into the search bar of the platform you use and skim the results — if the posts are years old or off-topic, drop it and ask the AI for a replacement.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You stop losing Sunday evenings to "what do I post tomorrow?" The week is planned in one sitting, and the rest of your time goes back to running the business.
- **For your business or work:** You show up consistently online, which is what algorithms and customers reward — even if each post is short, regular presence beats occasional perfect posts.
- **If you're just getting started:** Do this routine for two weeks in a row. By week three, you'll have a pattern you can copy-paste from last week, and the AI becomes a 10-minute helper instead of a 30-minute project.

## Try it now
Open your AI assistant right now and write a three-sentence brief about your business — what you sell, who buys it, and one theme for next week. Send it and ask for seven posts. That's the whole first run; everything else is editing.
